title: Preserve 1D Series for extension-dtype bounds in DataFrame.clip to prevent object dtype degradation
answers: Why does DataFrame.clip turn columns into object dtype when using an ExtensionArray bound?
How do I clip a DataFrame using an Int64 or extension-dtype array bound without degrading dtypes?
Why does DataFrame.clip raise TypeError or ValueError: Must specify axis=0 or 1 with an array bound?
body:
Symptom: DataFrame.clip with an extension-dtype array or Index bound converts columns to object dtype, raises TypeError on inplace=True, or raises ValueError: Must specify axis=0 or 1 when axis is None.
Root cause: pandas/core/frame.py:DataFrame._align_for_op broadcasts 1D Series operands to 2D DataFrames via _maybe_align_series_as_frame, but DataFrame.where only supports EA operands along 1D, and pandas/core/generic.py:NDFrame._clip_with_one_bound passed axis=None to where.
Fix pattern: Skip 2D frame broadcasting in _align_for_op when flex=None to keep the operand 1D, and normalize axis to 1 in _clip_with_one_bound when where receives an aligned Series with axis=None.
Constraints: Applies to DataFrame.clip and alignment callers passing flex=None; flex binary arithmetic and comparison operations require flex=True/False and must continue broadcasting to 2D frames.
applies: pandas DataFrame.clip and _align_for_op when aligning non-Series bounds with flex=None
